biomarker_basic.name: biomarker_basic
biomarker_basic.body_sql:
SELECT
  id,
  gene_symbol,
  biomarker_description,
  biomarker_id,
  test_is_a_panel
FROM biomarker

params.description: Provides one-row-per-biomarker basic attributes (id, gene symbol, description, biomarker identifier, and whether its test is a panel).
params.when_to_use: Lookup a biomarker by id to get its human-readable attributes | Display a list of biomarkers with basic metadata (gene_symbol, description, biomarker_id, test_is_a_panel) | Join biomarker attributes onto other result sets (e.g., results, tests, or joins to diseases) when you need descriptive columns but not aggregated measures | Compose into broader queries where biomarkers are the driving grain (one row per biomarker) and additional measures will be added after correct joins/aggregations
params.output_schema: id: unique biomarker identifier (derived directly from biomarker.id) | gene_symbol: gene symbol associated with the biomarker (derived directly from biomarker.gene_symbol) | biomarker_description: textual description of the biomarker (derived directly from biomarker.biomarker_description) | biomarker_id: external or alternate identifier for the biomarker (derived directly from biomarker.biomarker_id) | test_is_a_panel: boolean/flag indicating whether the related test is a panel (derived directly from biomarker.test_is_a_panel)
params.metric: No aggregated/derived numeric metrics in this view; all outputs are pass-through columns from the biomarker table. (If a metric is required by downstream composition, compute it after cardinality-safe joins or by re-aggregating after joining one-to-many tables.)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to biomarker_fda_test_basic on biomarker.id = biomarker_fda_test_basic.biomarker_id — safe because biomarker_basic is one-row-per-biomarker (one row per biomarker.id) and biomarker_fda_test_basic must be assessed for its own cardinality; only safe if biomarker_fda_test_basic is known to be one-row-per-biomarker as well. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to disease_basic or anatomical_entity_basic only when using those views as dimensions (e.g., to associate a biomarker with a single disease/anatomical_entity key) — safe if the join uses keys that are one-to-one or many-to-one from biomarker to the other view. Confirm the target view's grain before joining. | do NOT join directly to one-to-many tables/views (for example, differential_expression_results or disease_mutation_basic) without re-aggregation, because those are typically many rows per biomarker and will multiply biomarker_basic rows/measures. Instead: first aggregate the one-to-many table to one row per biomarker.id (e.g., COUNT(*), AVG(...), MAX(...)) and then join the aggregated result to biomarker_basic on biomarker.id to preserve correct cardinality. | When composing metrics that count or sum events related to biomarkers (from sibling views like differential_expression_results), compute those metrics in the sibling source (grouped by biomarker.id) and then join the grouped result to this view on biomarker.id to avoid duplication. | If you must join a raw one-to-many child table without pre-aggregation, use DISTINCT ON biomarker.id or windowing to reduce to one row per biomarker before combining, but prefer explicit aggregation to keep semantics clear.

biomarker_basic.description: Normalized projection of the biomarker table exposing core descriptive attributes and canonical keys. Use when questions need biomarker metadata, gene symbol, panel flag, or to join to alias/article/link tables. | Use for: list biomarkers and their gene symbols; count biomarkers flagged as panels vs single-gene; join biomarkers to aliases, articles, or FDA records
validated_on: Get a list of all biomarker descriptions
Show me biomarker titles and qa states for biomarker in phase Two
Show the gene symbol and the description of cancer biomarkers which are not in a panel
counter_examples: Show biomarker gene symbol and description for 'breast cancer'
Show me the description of all biomarkers

biomarker_fda_test_basic.name: biomarker_fda_test_basic
biomarker_fda_test_basic.body_sql:
SELECT
  test_trade_name,
  test_manufacturer,
  test_submission,
  biomarker_origin,
  doid,
  histological_type,
  specimen_type,
  platform_method,
  test_number_genes,
  test_adoption_evidence,
  test_approval_status,
  test_study_design,
  clinical_significance
FROM biomarker_fda_test

params.description: Provides one-row-per-test (grouped by test_trade_name and test_submission) FDA biomarker test attributes so you can report test metadata and compose further analysis without duplicating measures.
params.when_to_use: List or filter FDA biomarker tests and their attributes (manufacturer, submission id, origin, disease/DOID, histology, specimen, platform, gene count, evidence, approval, study design, clinical significance). | Join test-level metadata to other tables (e.g., results, diseases, anatomical entities) when you need one row per test and to preserve test granularity. | Aggregate counts or rates of tests by any of the output attributes (e.g., tests per manufacturer, tests by approval status). | Serve as the base for further SQL that composes test metadata with sibling views (disease_basic, biomarker_basic, etc.) ensuring cardinality-safe joins when done correctly.
params.output_schema: test_trade_name: trade name of the FDA biomarker test; derived from biomarker_fda_test.test_trade_name | test_manufacturer: name of the company/manufacturer who submitted the test; derived from biomarker_fda_test.test_manufacturer | test_submission: submission identifier for the test (e.g., FDA submission ID); derived from biomarker_fda_test.test_submission | biomarker_origin: origin/type of biomarker used in the test (e.g., somatic, germline); derived from biomarker_fda_test.biomarker_origin | doid: Disease Ontology ID linked to this test's disease indication; derived from biomarker_fda_test.doid | histological_type: histological classification associated with the test indication; derived from biomarker_fda_test.histological_type | specimen_type: specimen / sample type required or used by the test; derived from biomarker_fda_test.specimen_type | platform_method: platform or laboratory method used (e.g., NGS panel, IHC); derived from biomarker_fda_test.platform_method | test_number_genes: reported number of genes included in the test/panel; derived from biomarker_fda_test.test_number_genes | test_adoption_evidence: evidence level for clinical adoption of the test; derived from biomarker_fda_test.test_adoption_evidence | test_approval_status: regulatory approval status of the test; derived from biomarker_fda_test.test_approval_status | test_study_design: study design / evidence type used in submission (e.g., clinical trial type); derived from biomarker_fda_test.test_study_design | clinical_significance: stated clinical significance or interpretation for the test; derived from biomarker_fda_test.clinical_significance
params.grounded_columns: biomarker_fda_test.test_trade_name | biomarker_fda_test.test_manufacturer | biomarker_fda_test.test_submission | biomarker_fda_test.biomarker_origin | biomarker_fda_test.doid | biomarker_fda_test.histological_type | biomarker_fda_test.specimen_type | biomarker_fda_test.platform_method | biomarker_fda_test.test_number_genes | biomarker_fda_test.test_adoption_evidence | biomarker_fda_test.test_approval_status | biomarker_fda_test.test_study_design | biomarker_fda_test.clinical_significance
params.metric: No aggregated metrics are defined in this view; all output columns are passed-through base attributes. If you derive metrics from this view, compute them explicitly, for example: | tests_count = COUNT(*) -- counts rows (one row per test_trade_name, test_submission grain) | distinct_manufacturers = COUNT(DISTINCT test_manufacturer)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to disease_basic on disease_basic.doid = biomarker_fda_test_basic.doid — safe because biomarker_fda_test_basic is one-row-per-(test_trade_name, test_submission) and disease_basic is one-row-per-doid, so joining adds disease attributes without multiplying test rows. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to biomarker_basic on biomarker_basic.test_trade_name = biomarker_fda_test_basic.test_trade_name — safe only if biomarker_basic is one-row-per-test_trade_name; verify biomarker_basic's grain before joining. If biomarker_basic is many-to-one (multiple biomarker rows per trade name), aggregate biomarker_basic first (e.g., pick distinct attributes or aggregate) to avoid duplicating test rows. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to anatomical_entity_basic on anatomical_entity_basic.anatomical_entity_id = biomarker_fda_test_basic.specimen_type — safe if anatomical_entity_basic is one-row-per-specimen identifier (lookup/dimension). | DO NOT join directly to differential_expression_results or disease_mutation_basic (or any one-to-many result tables) on keys like test_trade_name or doid without re-aggregation, because those tables typically hold multiple result rows per test or disease. Doing so will multiply the one-row-per-test measures. Instead: |  - If you need aggregated result metrics per test, first aggregate the many-to-many table to the same key (test_trade_name, test_submission) and then join the aggregated metric back to this view. |  - Alternatively, join this view to the result table and then GROUP BY biomarker_fda_test_basic.test_trade_name, biomarker_fda_test_basic.test_submission to re-establish the intended grain before computing aggregates. | General rule: safe joins are to dimension/lookup tables that are unique on the join key (doid lookup, manufacturer lookup, specimen lookup). Avoid joining to tables where the joined side has multiple rows per (test_trade_name, test_submission) unless you aggregate the many side first or re-group to the test grain.

biomarker_fda_test_basic.description: Canonical projection of FDA test records exposing trade name, submission id, manufacturer, disease id (doid), platform, specimen and approval status. Use when analyzing FDA test attributes or joining to FDA-drug/trial/link tables. | Use for: summarize FDA tests by manufacturer or approval status; filter tests by disease (doid) or specimen type; join tests to trials, drugs, or biomarker_fda master records
validated_on: In how many fda test trials was test manufacturer 'ABBOTT MOLECULAR INC' involved?
counter_examples: List the platform method an the test study design for FDA tests from test manufacturer Dako Denmark A/S
What is the test trade name for FDA tests which are actually used for predisposition?

disease_basic.name: disease_basic

params.description: Provides one-row-per-disease identifier and canonical name for use as a stable disease dimension.
params.when_to_use: Look up disease id and human-readable disease name for reporting or labeling | Use as the disease dimension when composing aggregated metrics by disease | Join to other tables/views to enrich disease-level results (ensure cardinality-safety as noted) | Filter or group analytical queries by disease id or name
params.output_schema: id: disease primary identifier — derives from disease.id | name: canonical disease name — derives from disease.name
params.metric: No derived metrics in this view; all outputs are raw columns (id, name) directly selected from base table.
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to this view from fact/measurement tables on disease.id — safe because disease_basic is one-row-per-disease (grain = ['id']), so joining a fact table that has many rows per disease will not duplicate disease_basic rows but will expand facts per disease as expected. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to other one-row-per-disease sibling dimension/views (if any) such as disease-level summary views that also have grain ['id'] on id — safe because both are 1:1 at disease id and will not duplicate measures. | do NOT join without care to one-to-many tables/views (e.g., any table that stores multiple biomarker measurements, mutation events, tests, or differential expression rows per disease) directly into an aggregation that assumes disease_basic's row uniqueness — such joins will multiply disease-level counts/metrics. Instead, either: | - pre-aggregate the one-to-many table to disease-level (GROUP BY disease_id) before joining to disease_basic, or | - perform the join from the many-side (fact table) to disease_basic and then aggregate after the join, ensuring you aggregate on disease.id to restore disease-level granularity. | explicit examples of unsafe joins (must re-aggregate): do NOT join disease_basic directly to differential_expression_results or disease_mutation_basic without aggregation because those sibling views represent many rows per disease and would duplicate disease_basic when used as the driving table for metrics.

disease_basic.description: Projection of disease table exposing id and name. Use to resolve disease names from doid foreign keys and for joins to tests, mutations, and other disease-linked data. | Use for: resolve disease names for DOIDs; join disease metadata to tests or mutations
validated_on: Return the symbol and p-value for the expression of EGFR in lung cancer
Show name of diseases where the gene expression with symbol A1BG has a statistical significance of 'Yes'
counter_examples: Show all information about diseases where the name contains 'cancer'
Show name of diseases where the A1BG gene expression is statistically significant

anatomical_entity_basic.name: anatomical_entity_basic
anatomical_entity_basic.body_sql:
SELECT
  id,
  name,
  description
FROM anatomical_entity

params.description: Provides one-row-per-anatomical entity identifiers with their canonical name and textual description.
params.when_to_use: Look up an anatomical entity's name or description by id | Annotate or join experimental results with anatomical entity display fields | Compose into larger queries that need a de-duplicated list of anatomical entities (e.g., counts, groupings) as a dimension table
params.output_schema: id: unique identifier for the anatomical entity — derived from anatomical_entity.id | name: canonical display name of the anatomical entity — derived from anatomical_entity.name | description: textual description or definition of the anatomical entity — derived from anatomical_entity.description
params.metric: No derived metrics are produced by this view; all outputs are base columns (id, name, description). If a consumer needs an aggregate, compute it on top of this view, e.g., anatomical_entity_count = COUNT(anatomical_entity_basic.id) GROUP BY <dimension>.
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to fact or many-side tables/views on anatomical_entity.id — safe to join as a dimension (one-to-many) because anatomical_entity_basic is one-row-per-id and will not duplicate its own rows; e.g., JOIN differential_expression_results der ON der.anatomical_entity_id = anatomical_entity_basic.id — this is safe because anatomical_entity_basic is 1:1 per id and any multiplicity comes from the fact table, which is expected. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to disease_basic or biomarker_basic on keys only if those joins are logically one-to-one or many-to-one from the other side — e.g., if another view references anatomical_entity.id as a foreign key, joining anatomical_entity_basic on that key will not duplicate anatomical_entity_basic rows. | Do NOT join to one-to-many child tables/views (e.g., a hypothetical anatomical_entity_synonyms table or any result set that can contain multiple rows per anatomical_entity.id) without re-aggregating the child side first, because such joins would multiply anatomical_entity_basic rows and any aggregates computed before the join would be inflated. Instead, aggregate the child table to one row per anatomical_entity.id (e.g., STRING_AGG(synonym) or COUNT(*) GROUP BY anatomical_entity_id) and then join. | When composing metrics that count anatomical entities, compute COUNT(anatomical_entity_basic.id) from this view (or COUNT(DISTINCT anatomical_entity_basic.id) if joining to many-side tables) to avoid double-counting. | Avoid joining anatomical_entity_basic to another dimension table that is itself one-row-per-anatomical-entity on non-identical keys without validating uniqueness — only join on the explicit key anatomical_entity.id to preserve row uniqueness.

anatomical_entity_basic.description: Projection of anatomical entities exposing id, name, and description. Use to describe tissues/organs referenced by uberon_anatomical_id across tables (biomarker_edrn, cancer_tissue, healthy_expression). | Use for: describe tissues referenced by uberon ids; join anatomical descriptions to expression or biomarker data
validated_on: Show me biomarker titles and qa states for biomarker in phase Two

differential_expression_results.name: differential_expression_results
differential_expression_results.body_sql:
SELECT
  gene_symbol,
  doid,
  log2fc,
  pvalue,
  adjpvalue,
  statistical_significance,
  expression_change_direction,
  subjects_up,
  subjects_down,
  subjects_nochange,
  subjects_nocoverage,
  subjects_total
FROM differential_expression

params.description: Per-gene × per-disease differential expression results summarizing effect size, significance, direction, and subject-level counts.
params.when_to_use: Retrieve differential expression statistics (log2 fold change, p-value, adjusted p-value, significance) for a given gene and disease (DOID). | Filter or rank genes by effect size, significance, or direction for a specific disease or set of diseases. | Join expression summary results to gene- or disease-level metadata (e.g., to annotate results with gene symbols or disease names) without changing aggregate counts. | Compose higher-level aggregate reports that re-aggregate per-gene×disease results (for example, count of significant genes per disease) by treating this view as the atomic grain.
params.output_schema: gene_symbol: Official gene symbol string — derived directly from differential_expression.gene_symbol | doid: Disease Ontology ID (DOID) string — derived directly from differential_expression.doid | log2fc: Log2 fold change numeric — derived directly from differential_expression.log2fc | pvalue: Nominal p-value numeric for the differential expression test — derived directly from differential_expression.pvalue | adjpvalue: Multiple-testing adjusted p-value numeric (e.g., FDR) — derived directly from differential_expression.adjpvalue | statistical_significance: Boolean or categorical indicator denoting whether the test passed a significance threshold (as stored) — derived directly from differential_expression.statistical_significance | expression_change_direction: Categorical indicator of direction (e.g., 'up', 'down', 'no_change') — derived directly from differential_expression.expression_change_direction | subjects_up: Integer count of subjects/samples classified as 'up' for this gene×disease — derived directly from differential_expression.subjects_up | subjects_down: Integer count of subjects/samples classified as 'down' for this gene×disease — derived directly from differential_expression.subjects_down | subjects_nochange: Integer count of subjects/samples classified as 'no change' for this gene×disease — derived directly from differential_expression.subjects_nochange | subjects_nocoverage: Integer count of subjects/samples with no coverage for this gene (not measured) — derived directly from differential_expression.subjects_nocoverage | subjects_total: Integer total number of subjects/samples considered for this gene×disease — derived directly from differential_expression.subjects_total
params.grounded_columns: differential_expression.gene_symbol | differential_expression.doid | differential_expression.log2fc | differential_expression.pvalue | differential_expression.adjpvalue | differential_expression.statistical_significance | differential_expression.expression_change_direction | differential_expression.subjects_up | differential_expression.subjects_down | differential_expression.subjects_nochange | differential_expression.subjects_nocoverage | differential_expression.subjects_total
params.metric: log2fc = differential_expression.log2fc | pvalue = differential_expression.pvalue | adjpvalue = differential_expression.adjpvalue | statistical_significance = differential_expression.statistical_significance | expression_change_direction = differential_expression.expression_change_direction | subjects_up = differential_expression.subjects_up | subjects_down = differential_expression.subjects_down | subjects_nochange = differential_expression.subjects_nochange | subjects_nocoverage = differential_expression.subjects_nocoverage | subjects_total = differential_expression.subjects_total
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to gene-level dimension views (for example biomarker_basic) on gene_symbol — safe because this view is one row per (gene_symbol, doid). Joining on gene_symbol to a one-row-per-gene view (biomarker_basic) will not duplicate differential_expression measures. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to disease-level dimension views (for example disease_basic) on doid — safe because disease_basic is expected to be one row per DOID and differential_expression is one row per (gene_symbol, doid); joining on doid preserves the one-row-per-(gene,disease) grain and does not duplicate measures. | do NOT join directly (without aggregation) to known one-to-many children of the differential experiment that enumerate subjects/samples or measurements (for example a raw sample-level table) because those joins would multiply counts/metrics (subjects_* and subjects_total) across the expanded rows. If you must join to a one-to-many table, first aggregate that table to the (gene_symbol, doid) grain (e.g., SUM/COUNT per gene_symbol, doid) and then join to this view. | do NOT join to sibling multi-row views that contain multiple rows per gene_symbol (or per doid) such as a table of isoforms, probe-level measurements, or repeated tests, unless you re-aggregate after the join. Such joins would produce duplicated log2fc/pvalue rows and invalidate significance and subject counts. | When composing metrics across diseases (for example, count of significant genes per disease), use this view as the atomic input and apply appropriate aggregations (COUNT(*) FILTER (statistical_significance = true), AVG(log2fc), etc.) — these operations are safe because you are aggregating from the view's defined grain. | If joining to sibling views listed (biomarker_basic, biomarker_fda_test_basic, disease_basic, anatomical_entity_basic, disease_mutation_basic), prefer joins on their canonical keys (gene_symbol for biomarker_* views; doid for disease_basic) and ensure those sibling views are one-row-per-key to avoid unintended duplication. If a sibling view is multi-row per key, re-aggregate it first.

differential_expression_results.description: Projection of differential expression results per gene_symbol and disease (doid), exposing effect size, p-values, direction and subject counts. Use for filtering significant genes, joining to gene or disease metadata, or aggregating counts of up/down genes. | Use for: list significantly differentially expressed genes for a disease; compute counts of up/down-regulated genes; join differential expression to disease names or gene metadata

disease_mutation_basic.name: disease_mutation_basic
disease_mutation_basic.body_sql:
SELECT
  id,
  chromosome_id,
  chromosome_pos,
  ref_nt,
  alt_nt,
  ensembl_transcript_id,
  cds_pos,
  peptide_pos,
  aa_pos_uniprotkb,
  ref_aa,
  alt_aa,
  mutation_freq,
  data_source,
  doid
FROM disease_mutation

params.description: Provides one-row-per-mutation details for disease-associated genetic variants (genomic position, alleles, transcript/protein positions, frequency, source, and linked disease DOID).
params.when_to_use: Look up details for a specific mutation id (id) or list of mutation ids. | Filter or aggregate mutations by chromosome, position, transcript, peptide/protein position, or linked disease (doid). | Join mutation-level attributes into larger analyses (e.g., join with disease, biomarker, or expression data) where each mutation should remain one row. | Serve as the base relation when composing additional SQL that computes counts, distinct counts, or summary statistics of mutations.
params.output_schema: id: Unique identifier of the mutation record — derived directly from disease_mutation.id | chromosome_id: Chromosome identifier (e.g., '1', 'X') — derived directly from disease_mutation.chromosome_id | chromosome_pos: Genomic coordinate (position) on the chromosome — derived directly from disease_mutation.chromosome_pos | ref_nt: Reference nucleotide(s) at the genomic position — derived directly from disease_mutation.ref_nt | alt_nt: Alternate nucleotide(s) for the mutation — derived directly from disease_mutation.alt_nt | ensembl_transcript_id: Ensembl transcript identifier that the mutation maps to — derived directly from disease_mutation.ensembl_transcript_id | cds_pos: Coding DNA sequence position (cds coordinate) for the mutation on the transcript — derived directly from disease_mutation.cds_pos | peptide_pos: Peptide position (amino-acid position on the canonical peptide) — derived directly from disease_mutation.peptide_pos | aa_pos_uniprotkb: Amino-acid position in UniProtKB coordinate system (if provided) — derived directly from disease_mutation.aa_pos_uniprotkb | ref_aa: Reference amino acid at the protein position — derived directly from disease_mutation.ref_aa | alt_aa: Alternate amino acid resulting from the mutation — derived directly from disease_mutation.alt_aa | mutation_freq: Observed frequency or prevalence metric for this mutation (as stored) — derived directly from disease_mutation.mutation_freq | data_source: Source or provenance of the mutation record (database or study) — derived directly from disease_mutation.data_source | doid: Disease Ontology ID linking this mutation to a disease — derived directly from disease_mutation.doid
params.grounded_columns: disease_mutation.id | disease_mutation.chromosome_id | disease_mutation.chromosome_pos | disease_mutation.ref_nt | disease_mutation.alt_nt | disease_mutation.ensembl_transcript_id | disease_mutation.cds_pos | disease_mutation.peptide_pos | disease_mutation.aa_pos_uniprotkb | disease_mutation.ref_aa | disease_mutation.alt_aa | disease_mutation.mutation_freq | disease_mutation.data_source | disease_mutation.doid
params.metric: mutation_freq = disease_mutation.mutation_freq  -- this view surfaces the stored per-mutation frequency value (no aggregation) | row_grain = id  -- the view is one row per disease_mutation.id (no aggregation performed)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to disease_basic on disease_basic.doid = disease_mutation_basic.doid — safe because disease_basic (by its naming) is one row per disease (doid), so joining does NOT duplicate mutation rows. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to biomarker_basic on biomarker_basic.some_mutation_id = disease_mutation_basic.id ONLY IF biomarker_basic is known to be one-row-per-mutation; otherwise treat biomarker_basic as a potential one-to-many (not assumed safe). | do NOT join to differential_expression_results (or any other table that can contain multiple rows per mutation.id or per doid) without aggregation first, because those one-to-many joins will multiply mutation rows and thus duplicate mutation_freq and any counts derived directly from this view. | do NOT join to sibling tables that are one-to-many on id (for example, any experimental results, evidence lines, or citations linked to mutation.id) without either: (a) aggregating the many-side to one row per disease_mutation.id, or (b) explicitly selecting/limiting rows so that the join remains one-to-one. Otherwise measures such as mutation_freq will be duplicated. | When composing summaries (counts, distinct counts, aggregated frequencies) from this view combined with other tables, perform aggregation at the outer query level grouping by the desired keys (e.g., ensembl_transcript_id, doid) rather than relying on implicit de-duplication via joins.

disease_mutation_basic.description: Normalized projection of disease mutations exposing genomic coordinates, transcript/protein positions, alleles, frequency, source and linked disease (doid). Use when analyzing mutation counts, joining to articles/predictions, or mapping to proteins. | Use for: list mutations for a disease; join mutations to articles, impact predictions, or tissue annotations; map mutations to proteins/transcripts
validated_on: Show me all disease mutations
Show all information about disease mutations

disease_mutation_with_articles.name: disease_mutation_with_articles
disease_mutation_with_articles.body_sql:
SELECT
  dm.id,
  dm.chromosome_id,
  dm.chromosome_pos,
  dm.ref_nt,
  dm.alt_nt,
  dm.ensembl_transcript_id,
  dm.cds_pos,
  dm.peptide_pos,
  dm.aa_pos_uniprotkb,
  dm.ref_aa,
  dm.alt_aa,
  dm.mutation_freq,
  dm.data_source,
  dm.doid,
  dma.pmid
FROM disease_mutation AS dm

disease_mutation_with_articles.description: Denormalized disease mutation rows with linked article PMIDs (one row per mutation x article). Useful to filter or rank mutations by literature support.

disease_mutation_with_predictions.name: disease_mutation_with_predictions
disease_mutation_with_predictions.body_sql:
SELECT
  dm.id,
  dm.chromosome_id,
  dm.chromosome_pos,
  dm.ref_nt,
  dm.alt_nt,
  dm.ensembl_transcript_id,
  dm.cds_pos,
  dm.peptide_pos,
  dm.aa_pos_uniprotkb,
  dm.ref_aa,
  dm.alt_aa,
  dm.mutation_freq,
  dm.data_source,
  dm.doid,
  dpi.id AS "disease_mutation_impact_prediction.id",
  dpi.site_prediction AS "disease_mutation_impact_prediction.site_prediction",
  dpi.probability AS "disease_mutation_impact_prediction.probability",
  dpi.tool AS "disease_mutation_impact_prediction.tool"
FROM
  disease_mutation dm
JOIN
  disease_mutation_impact_prediction dpi
ON
  dm.id = dpi.disease_mutation_id
disease_mutation_with_predictions.description: Disease mutation rows joined to impact prediction rows (one row per mutation x prediction). Useful for filtering or aggregating by predicted impact, tool, or probability.

  COUNT(DISTINCT test_submission) AS distinct_test_count,
  AVG(test_number_genes::double precision) AS avg_test_number_genes,
  COUNT(DISTINCT test_trade_name) AS distinct_trade_name_count
FROM biomarker_fda_test_basic
GROUP BY test_manufacturer
ORDER BY test_manufacturer
fda_test_by_manufacturer.description: Aggregated measures of FDA tests grouped by test_manufacturer. Provides counts of distinct tests and basic distributions useful for summaries and rankings by manufacturer.

fda_test_manufacturer_normalized.name: fda_test_manufacturer_normalized
fda_test_manufacturer_normalized.body_sql:
SELECT
  /* lift literal columns out of the view: none needed beyond table columns */
  bft.test_submission AS test_submission,
  bft.test_trade_name AS test_trade_name,
  -- canonicalize manufacturer: trim whitespace, treat empty-string as NULL, normalize internal spacing
  NULLIF(
    regexp_replace(
      bft.test_manufacturer::text,              -- ensure text for regex ops
      '\s+',                                    -- collapse multiple whitespace
      ' ',                                      -- to single space
      'g'
    )::text,
    ''                                          -- convert empty string to NULL
  ) AS test_manufacturer_canonical
FROM
  biomarker_fda_test bft
fda_test_manufacturer_normalized.description: Normalized/cleaned projection of biomarker_fda_test to canonicalize manufacturer names (trim, NULL handling) and expose stable keys for joins.

species_rows.name: species_rows

species_by_genus_projection.name: species_by_genus_projection

healthy_expression_by_species_anatomy.name: healthy_expression_by_species_anatomy
healthy_expression_by_species_anatomy.body_sql:
SELECT
  he.ensembl_gene_id,

disease_mutation_with_tissue_and_article.name: disease_mutation_with_tissue_and_articles
disease_mutation_with_tissue_and_article.body_sql:
SELECT

  dm.alt_nt,

mutation_transcript_protein_map.name: mutation_transcript_protein_map

mutation_transcript_protein_map.description: Mapping of disease mutation transcript identifiers to protein identifiers (uniprot) via map_protein_disease_mutation and map_uniprot_canonical_id. One row per disease_mutation.enembl_transcript_id mapped to a uniprot canonical accession where available.

fda_test_trial_with_test.name: fda_test_trial_with_test

biomarker_edrn_type_normalized.name: biomarker_edrn_type_normalized
biomarker_edrn_type_normalized.body_sql:
SELECT
  be.id,
  be.qa_state,
  be.biomarker_title,
  -- normalized: lower-case trimmed biomarker_type
  lower(trim(be.biomarker_type)) AS biomarker_type_normalized,
  -- is_protein_type flag: true when normalized type equals 'protein' OR contains 'protein' as a whole word
  (
    lower(trim(be.biomarker_type)) = 'protein'
    OR lower(trim(be.biomarker_type)) ~ '\mprotein\M'
  ) AS is_protein_type,
  be.uberon_anatomical_id,
  be.phase
FROM biomarker_edrn be
biomarker_edrn_type_normalized.description: Normalized/cleaned biomarker_edrn projection: canonicalizes biomarker_type to lower-case trimmed string and exposes a boolean flag for protein type. Keeps one row per biomarker_edrn.id for reliable downstream filtering and grouping.

biomarker_edrn_canonical_types.name: biomarker_edrn_canonical_types
biomarker_edrn_canonical_types.body_sql:
SELECT
  id,
  qa_state,
  biomarker_title,
  -- canonicalize biomarker_type: trim, lower, map common synonyms to normalized terms
  CASE
    WHEN biomarker_type IS NULL OR trim(both ' ' FROM biomarker_type) = '' THEN NULL
    WHEN lower(trim(both ' ' FROM biomarker_type)) IN (
      'protein', 'protein biomarker', 'protein-based', 'proteomic'
    ) THEN 'protein'
    WHEN lower(trim(both ' ' FROM biomarker_type)) IN (
      'dna', 'dna biomarker', 'genomic', 'genetic', 'dna-based', 'nucleic acid'
    ) THEN 'dna'
    WHEN lower(trim(both ' ' FROM biomarker_type)) IN (
      'rna', 'mrna', 'microrna', 'rna-based', 'transcriptomic'
    ) THEN 'rna'
    WHEN lower(trim(both ' ' FROM biomarker_type)) IN (
      'metabolite', 'metabolic', 'metabolomic'
    ) THEN 'metabolite'
    WHEN lower(trim(both ' ' FROM biomarker_type)) IN (
      'imaging', 'radiologic', 'radiographic', 'imaging biomarker'
    ) THEN 'imaging'
    WHEN lower(trim(both ' ' FROM biomarker_type)) IN (
      'clinical', 'clinical marker', 'clinical assay'
    ) THEN 'clinical'
    WHEN lower(trim(both ' ' FROM biomarker_type)) IN (
      'antibody', 'antibodies'
    ) THEN 'antibody'
    WHEN lower(trim(both ' ' FROM biomarker_type)) IN (
      'protein fragment', 'peptide', 'peptidic'
    ) THEN 'peptide'
    ELSE lower(trim(both ' ' FROM biomarker_type))
  END AS biomarker_type_canonical,
  uberon_anatomical_id,
  -- canonicalize phase: trim, lower, normalize common phase notations
  CASE
    WHEN phase IS NULL OR trim(both ' ' FROM phase) = '' THEN NULL
    WHEN lower(trim(both ' ' FROM phase)) IN ('preclinical', 'pre-clinical', 'pre clinical') THEN 'preclinical'
    WHEN lower(trim(both ' ' FROM phase)) IN ('i', 'phase i', 'phase 1', '1') THEN 'phase i'
    WHEN lower(trim(both ' ' FROM phase)) IN ('ii', 'phase ii', 'phase 2', '2') THEN 'phase ii'
    WHEN lower(trim(both ' ' FROM phase)) IN ('iii', 'phase iii', 'phase 3', '3') THEN 'phase iii'
    WHEN lower(trim(both ' ' FROM phase)) IN ('iv', 'phase iv', 'phase 4', '4') THEN 'phase iv'
    WHEN lower(trim(both ' ' FROM phase)) IN ('pilot', 'feasibility') THEN 'pilot'
    WHEN lower(trim(both ' ' FROM phase)) IN ('na', 'n/a', 'none', 'not applicable') THEN 'not applicable'
    WHEN lower(trim(both ' ' FROM phase)) IN ('approved', 'approval') THEN 'approved'
    WHEN lower(trim(both ' ' FROM phase)) IN ('investigational', 'experimental') THEN 'investigational'
    ELSE lower(trim(both ' ' FROM phase))
  END AS phase_canonical
FROM biomarker_edrn
biomarker_edrn_canonical_types.description: Normalized canonicalization/cleaning of biomarker_type and phase fields for consistent filtering (trim, lower-case, map common synonyms). One row per biomarker_edrn.id.

biomarker_edrn_canonicalized.name: biomarker_edrn_canonicalized
biomarker_edrn_canonicalized.body_sql:
SELECT
  id,
  -- canonicalized title: trim surrounding whitespace and collapse internal runs of whitespace to single space
  NULLIF(regexp_replace(trim(biomarker_title), '\s+', ' ', 'g'), '') AS biomarker_title,
  -- canonicalized type: trim and lower for normalization, keep NULL if empty
  NULLIF(lower(trim(biomarker_type)), '') AS biomarker_type,
  -- canonicalized phase: trim, uppercase canonical forms (I, II, III, IV) where possible, otherwise keep trimmed value
  CASE
    WHEN biomarker_edrn.phase IS NULL THEN NULL
    ELSE
      NULLIF(
        CASE
          WHEN regexp_replace(upper(trim(biomarker_edrn.phase)), '[^IVX0-9]+', '', 'g') IN ('I','II','III','IV','V') THEN regexp_replace(upper(trim(biomarker_edrn.phase)), '[^IVX0-9]+', '', 'g')
          WHEN upper(trim(biomarker_edrn.phase)) ~ 'PHASE\s*I{1,3}' THEN regexp_replace(upper(trim(biomarker_edrn.phase)), '.*(I{1,3}).*', '\1', 'g')
          WHEN upper(trim(biomarker_edrn.phase)) ~ 'PHASE\s*IV' THEN 'IV'
          ELSE trim(biomarker_edrn.phase)
        END
      , '')
  END AS phase,
  -- qa_state normalized: trim and convert empty to NULL
  NULLIF(trim(qa_state), '') AS qa_state,
  -- uberon id: trim and convert empty to NULL
  NULLIF(trim(uberon_anatomical_id), '') AS uberon_anatomical_id
FROM biomarker_edrn
biomarker_edrn_canonicalized.description: Normalized/projection of biomarker_edrn with trimmed/canonicalized textual fields and explicit nullable handling for key descriptive columns. Useful when matching types/phase values or presenting titles consistently.
